explanation: The heaviest operations reside in the local client-side LQFT Benchmark page and server database metrics. Running the browser benchmark inserts and searches N items across several simulated 32-way branching trie representations. Each transaction performs custom hashing and up to 6 levels of node lookups, yielding a linear O(N) CPU runtime with a structural multiplier (~60N). SWR caching in the frontend stores U unique JSON payloads to ensure O(1) page transitions, while AI chat payload truncation constrains history assembly. Server-side database actions on D documents scale logarithmically O(log D) due to compound compound indexes on visitor and path tables.
